diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepeat operations after insufficient progress, especially clicks, no-ops, and scrolling.
expected_mechanism: A progress-gated retry limit should force strategy changes instead of repeated actions, improving task progress while costing occasional extra replanning and potentially abandoning a retry that might eventually succeed.
policy_text: Track whether each action produces new task-relevant state. After two materially identical actions without new evidence or progress, do not repeat the action again; reassess the state and choose a different strategy, target, or interaction. Permit another retry only when new observations justify it.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(any(.stack_frames[]; .=="result:repeated")) | .value' samples.jsonl | awk '{if($1>0)p+=$1;else n+=-$1} END {printf "bad=%d good=%d excess=%+d ratio=%.2f\n",p,n,p-n,p/n}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated-operation samples: bad 1,485 versus good 224, an excess of +1,261 and a 6.63× bad/good ratio.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(any(.stack_frames[]; .=="result:repeated")) | [.value, (.stack_frames[]|select(startswith("action:")))] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($1>0)p[$2]+=$1;else n[$2]+=-$1} END {for(k in p) printf "%s bad=%d good=%d excess=%+d\n",k,p[k],n[k],p[k]-n[k]}' | sort
quantitative_evidence.finding: The largest repeated-action excesses were click +639 (679 vs 40), noop +356 (441 vs 85), and scroll +277 (278 vs 1).

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(any(.stack_frames[]; .=="result:repeated")) | [.labels.source_session[0], .value] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($2>0)ps[$1]=1;else ns[$1]=1} END {for(k in ps)p++;for(k in ns)n++;printf "bad_sessions=%d good_sessions=%d\n",p,n}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated behavior occurred across 88 bad-side source sessions versus 20 good-side source sessions, showing recurrence rather than a single-run outlier.
